mode: Independent actual screenshot review. Bee did not execute the runtime renderer or manipulate this comparison browser. Separate earlier UI play exists.
scope: 19 personally opened screenshots; not every image in the folder.
Director_quote: I use lines where needed for separation and I let the scene dictate how to render Trip's defined outlines vs implied boundaries.

findings.claim: Thin outer contour improves silhouette separation against unchanged white room while preserving shaded roundness.

Medium contour is more emphatic, but adds a continuous outer border rather than solving scene-selective boundaries. On desktop it reads more graphically enclosed; mobile stronger border remains useful evidence, not automatic final choice.

Forearm tip crossing the head remains soft/unmarked with both widths; emphasizing the outside contour does not resolve this inside overlap. No phone is rendered, so this is not a grip-recognition result.
First lighting pair makes broad body surfaces too gray for this Trip comparison. Its long ground shadow adds a different visible grounding cue.

Brighter rebalance restores white highlights with stronger rounded form. Lighting alone still lets some lit outer edges soften into the pale room. Thin contour plus brighter rebalance gives the strongest provisional balance of white identity, volume and readable silhouette among the reviewed samples.
The long cast shadow seen in the first lighting pair is not visible in the brighter pair. This review records that difference without attributing its implementation cause.

bounded_recommendation: Retain the brighter+thin result as a candidate for Director comparison, not a universal outline policy. Next rendering work should address where a crossing form needs selective boundary/light separation, with white material/accepted geometry held. Do not solve the overlap by merely thickening the entire outer line.
